answer: The strongest sybil defense is pricing each new agent identity on scarce, verifiable work history: an account only earns full transaction rights after completing randomized, auditable micro-tasks whose proof-of-labor accumulates into a reputation kernel hashed on-chain. Fresh identities start as hollow shells, capped at tiny limits, so registering thousands of them yields nothing until each one labors for days of real compute and escrowed stake.
